failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs six steps, each with a bar fixed before any data. A repeated situation on the nightly card becomes a draft, and your yes registers it. It is then tested on 2000-2023 against the strict pass mark, and survivors run as a paper book on live sessions for 20 recorded sessions. Only if it beats the random picks and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs, passes the check that no future data leaked in, and you say yes again is it admitted, and only then may the allocated capital use it (still paper; the final real-money gate is separate). Today no rule has been admitted yet, and the stock rules are still in the live paper stage. One thing that isn't right, sir: 2 options trades scored this week at an entry more than 0.1% from the decision's own (the widest: BANKNIFTY on 2026-11-17, decided at 61,559.95, scored at 61,741.05, 181 points apart); and on the crypto side, 39 NDAX coins cost more a side than the paper books charge (measured by the worker, 13 days): SAND 31.445% against 1.0%, VIRTUAL 7.253% against 0.6%, A 7.472% against 1.0%; the books against their random twins pay the same, so comparisons hold, but small coins' own results are flattered. Ask me what's wrong for the details.

problems.why: A simple process question gets about seven dense sentences, including a long unrelated tangent on options scoring and crypto fees with many figures.
Phrases like 'random twins', 'scored at an entry', 'the worker', 'a side' and 'NDAX coins' are unexplained, and the six steps are never laid out clearly for a beginner.
